acceptance_criteria: SSE stream working. State-change delivered <100ms. Typing suppression works. Keepalive cleans dead connections. Load test passes.
description:
## Why this issue exists

Chat without real-time push is polling. The JMAP Chat spec requires EventSource (RFC 8620 §7.3) for state-change delivery and defines typing and presence as ephemeral push events. Without push, clients must poll `Message/changes` on a timer — unusable for interactive chat.

## What needs to be done

### Phase 1 — JMAP EventSource (SSE) state-change events

RFC 8620 §7.3 defines the `/events` endpoint. When a client connects, it receives a stream of `StateChange` events whenever the server state for any of the client's subscribed types changes.

Implement `GET /jmap/events` (or the URL from the Session `eventSourceUrl` template):

- Accept `types` query parameter (comma-separated type names to watch; `*` for all)
- Accept `closeafter` and `ping` parameters per RFC 8620
- On connection, add the client to an in-memory subscriber set per account
- When the bridge layer or any `/set` method bumps a state token, notify all connected EventSource clients for that account
- Send:
  ```
  event: state
  data: {"@type":"StateChange","changed":{"<accountId>":{"Message":"<token>","Chat":"<token>","ChatContact":"<token>"}}}
  ```
- Send keepalive ping every 30 seconds (configurable) to detect dead connections
- On client disconnect, remove from subscriber set

Use a `tokio::sync::broadcast` channel per account; the SSE handler is the receiver, the bridge/set handlers are senders. Bounded channel; slow clients are dropped rather than causing backpressure.

### Phase 2 — Typing events

`Chat/typing` (defined in the methods epic) already accepts and validates the request. This phase wires up delivery.

When `Chat/typing` is called:
- Deliver a `typing` SSE event to all connected clients of this account (other than the requesting connection) for the given chatId:
  ```
  event: typing
  data: {"chatId":"<id>","senderId":"<contact-id>","typing":<bool>}
  ```
- Check each recipient client's `receiveTypingIndicators` for this chat; suppress delivery if false
- Not stored; not replayed on reconnect

The event is delivered only to local clients (owner's connected sessions). Delivering typing events to remote Delta Chat users is out of scope — Delta Chat has no equivalent server-to-server typing notification mechanism.

### Phase 3 — Presence events

When `PresenceStatus/set` updates the owner's presence:
- Deliver a `presence` SSE event to all connected clients of this account:
  ```
  event: presence
  data: {"contactId":"<owner-id>","presence":"<state>","lastActiveAt":"<ts>","statusText":"<string>|null","statusEmoji":"<string>|null"}
  ```

Presence propagation to remote peers (Delta Chat users or other JMAP Chat servers) is out of scope for v1.

### Phase 4 — JMAP push subscriptions (RFC 8620 §7.2) — stretch goal

RFC 8620 defines a `PushSubscription` mechanism for out-of-band push delivery (Web Push / VAPID). This enables mobile clients to receive notifications when not connected via EventSource.

- `PushSubscription/get`, `PushSubscription/set`, `PushSubscription/changes`
- On state change, POST to the client's `url` with the StateChange payload
- VAPID-sign the push message if the session advertises `urn:ietf:params:jmap:webpush-vapid`

Phase 4 is a stretch goal; Phases 1–3 are required for v1.

## Acceptance criteria

- `GET /jmap/events` returns a valid EventSource stream
- State-change event delivered to connected client within 100ms of a `Message/set` create
- Typing event delivered to other connected sessions of the same account
- `receiveTypingIndicators: false` suppresses typing delivery for that chat
- Keepalive ping sent on schedule; dead connections cleaned up
- Presence event delivered on `PresenceStatus/set` update
- Load test: 100 concurrent SSE connections on one account; all receive events without backpressure stall
design: tokio::sync::broadcast per account is the right primitive: fan-out to N connected clients, bounded buffer, slow receivers are dropped cleanly. The SSE endpoint is a long-lived axum handler that holds the broadcast receiver. State-change notifications are fire-and-forget from the writer side — the bridge and /set handlers do not wait for SSE delivery.
title: JMAP Chat: push and SSE
